retry_guidance.safe_always: GET requests; any request that failed before reaching the server (connection refused, DNS).
retry_guidance.safe_with_idempotency_key: start, whatsapp-send, the three template writes, email-send, email-batch, email-received-forward, the three menu writes, the four auto-attendant writes and every partner write, on a network error, 5xx, or 409 idempotency_in_progress, with the same key.

endpoints.title: Save the auto-attendant draft
endpoints.summary: For a connected app's key alone, with `chat:attendant` in its connection's grant: an application's own key, full access included, answers `403 insufficient_scope`, and builds its auto-attendant in the console. Replaces the whole draft with `menu` and answers it as stored, every choice with its `id`, and its `problems`. The draft reaches no customer until it is published. The console and the API share this one draft, and the last save wins. A draft may hold problems; `POST /v1/chat/attendant/publish` refuses them. Draft saves are not recorded in the client's account record, as in the console.
endpoints.auth_note: A connected app's key with chat:attendant in its connection's grant: the live key (tk_live_) an approved connection hands the app. A business's own key, full access included, answers 403 insufficient_scope with WWW-Authenticate naming chat:attendant; a partner key answers 401 unauthorized; a connection the client ended answers 401 unauthorized.

fields.name: menu

constraints.note: A menu that breaks a rule is saved with its problems; only its shape is refused.

fields.description: The menu: `opening` (the first message, up to 1024 characters), `list_button` (the list's button label, up to 20 characters; «القائمة» or Menu by default), `away` (the line sent outside the team's working hours instead of handing over, or null for Tawked's default; the hours are set in the console), `fallback` (sent when the customer writes instead of choosing, up to 1024 characters, or null for Tawked's default) and `choices`, up to 10. A choice is `{ id, title, description, action }`: `id` optional (`c_` then 4 to 12 lowercase letters or digits), `title` up to 20 characters as buttons (1 to 3 choices) or 24 as a list (4 to 10), `description` a list item's second line up to 72 characters or null. `action` is one of `{ "type": "reply", "text", "link" }` (the text, and an https link under it or null); `{ "type": "submenu", "text", "choices" }` (up to 10 choices, one level only; Tawked adds «رجوع» when there is room); `{ "type": "ask", "detail", "label", "question", "tag", "assign" }` (`detail` is `order_number`, `name`, `city` or `custom`, `label` for `custom` only: asks one detail, then hands the conversation to the team with the answer and the tag); `{ "type": "team", "line", "tag", "assign" }` (hands the conversation to the team; `line` is what the customer is told, or null); `{ "type": "radeef" }` (hands it to Radeef). `tag` is the label the conversation gets in Tawked Chat, 2 to 40 letters, digits, `_` or `-`; `assign` is `{ "mode": "auto" }`, Tawked Chat assigning as usual. The top level needs a `team` choice. Refused outright: `required`, `not_object`, `too_large` (over 64 KB or 256 choices in all).

body.message: `Idempotency-Key` must be 1-128 printable ASCII characters

fields.description: Optional on the four auto-attendant writes. See idempotency.attendant_writes.

request.notes: Replaces the whole draft, shared with the console: the last save wins. It reaches no customer until published.

response.notes: The menu as stored, every choice with its id.

delivery.waits_note: The first attempt goes at once; after a failed attempt n (n < 5) the next waits waits_seconds[n-1]. config tawked.webhooks.backoff_seconds holds [60,300,1800,7200,21600]; its last value is never reached.

delivery.duplicates: Every delivery carries the header tawked-webhook-id: one id per event, the same on every retry and on a delivery sent again from the console. Dedupe on it; on the body, dedupe on the event name, data.id and data.recipient.id when recipient is present (e-mail events of a message of several recipients), else the event name and data.id.

notes: Configured per application on its Webhooks page: a URL and a secret, revealed on demand and rotatable. An application a partner provisioned has no webhook of its own: its verification outcomes go to the partner's event log and, when the partner subscribed to them, to the partner webhook, with the partner's `external_id`.
`verification.verified` and `verification.failed` fire from `check`; `verification.expired` fires from the background expiry sweep, and from any `check` or `GET` that discovers the expiry itself.

Every delivery carries `tawked-timestamp`, `tawked-signature` (hex HMAC-SHA256 of `"{timestamp}.{raw body}"` with your secret), `tawked-event` and `tawked-webhook-id` (one id per event, the same on every retry: dedupe on it). Verify the signature against the raw request body before trusting any payload.

Delivery retries automatically with backoff on anything but a 2xx response, with the same job and schedule as partner webhooks; the exact retry count is below. The delivery log in the console shows every attempt.
The URL must be https on a public host, and your endpoint must answer itself: a redirect is not followed and counts as a failed attempt.

A test event sent from the console's Webhooks page is one sample `verification.verified` whose envelope also carries `"test": true`, with made-up values under `data`: an id of zeros, the reference `test-event`, the mode `test`. No real event carries `test`, so skip your own side effects when it is there.
An application with WhatsApp also receives `message.sent`, `message.delivered`, `message.read` and `message.failed` at the same URL, in the same envelope (see WhatsApp messages).

One event per status change, to the application's webhook URL, signed and retried exactly like `verification.*`: the same `tawked-timestamp`, `tawked-signature` and `tawked-event` headers, the same HMAC over `"{timestamp}.{raw body}"`, the same retry schedule, the same delivery log in the console.

The same envelope as `verification.*`: `event`, `data` and `sent_at`. The message's fields sit under `data`, with `occurred_at` the time of the status the event announces and `error` null unless the event is `message.failed` (then `{ "code", "message" }`). A test event from the console is always `verification.verified`, so no `message.*` event carries `test`.

Delivered by the status sync, which follows each message for 48 hours after the send. Only the status reached is announced: a message that jumps straight to `read` gets one `message.read`, not the rungs in between.
`to` is masked the way the console shows it. Keep your own copy of the destination next to the returned `id` or your `reference`.

One event per outcome per recipient, to the application's webhook URL, signed like `verification.*` and `message.*`: the same headers, the same HMAC over `"{timestamp}.{raw body}"` and the same delivery log, and retried longer (below).

The same envelope, `event`, `data` and `sent_at`, with `type` (equal to `event`) and `timestamp` (when the event happened) after `data`. For a message to one recipient sent in the original shape, `data` carries the message: `id`, `status`, `application_id`, `from`, `to`, `subject`, `reference`, `price_halalas`, `error` (`{ "code", "message" }` or null), `bounce` (`{ "type", "subtype" }` on a bounce, null otherwise), `occurred_at` and `created_at`.

For any other message, each recipient gets its own webhook: `data` adds, after `to`, `recipient` (`{ "id", "address", "type", "status" }`: `type` is `to`, `cc` or `bcc`) and `tags`; `to`, `error`, `bounce` and `occurred_at` are that recipient's, and `status` is the message's in the extended words. A recipient suppressed by the time the message was due gets `email.failed` with `error.code` `recipient_suppressed`.

Every delivery carries the header `tawked-webhook-id`: one id per event, the same on every retry and on a delivery sent again from the console. Dedupe on it. A receiver that dedupes on the body uses `event`, `data.id` and `data.recipient.id` when `recipient` is present, else `event` and `data.id`.
`to` and `recipient.address` carry the full address the message was sent to.

Every `email.*`, `domain.*` and `suppression.*` delivery carries `type` (equal to `event`) and `timestamp` (when it happened, ISO 8601 UTC with milliseconds) beside `event`, `data` and `sent_at`. A test-mode event adds `"mode": "test"`. Verification and WhatsApp events keep their envelope as it was.
`to` and `recipient.address` carry the full address.
Every delivery keeps the Tawked signature: `tawked-signature` is the hex HMAC-SHA256 of `"{tawked-timestamp}.{raw body}"` with the endpoint's Tawked secret.

Standard Webhooks signing adds `webhook-id` (the same value as `tawked-webhook-id`), `webhook-timestamp` (the same instant, in seconds) and `webhook-signature` (`v1,` and the base64 HMAC-SHA256 of `"{webhook-id}.{webhook-timestamp}.{raw body}"`, keyed with the base64-decoded part of the `whsec_` secret after its prefix). It is on for every endpoint created since this change; an older endpoint gets it when its owner turns it on (the Webhooks page, `PATCH /v1/webhooks/{id}` with `{"signing": {"standard_webhooks": true}}`, or `POST /v1/webhooks/{id}/rotate-secret`). Give the `whsec_` secret alone to a Standard Webhooks library.

`POST /v1/webhooks/{id}/rotate-secret` rotates the Standard secret by default: the previous one keeps signing beside the new one, space-separated in `webhook-signature`, for 24 hours. The Tawked secret rotates only when asked (`"scheme": "tawked"` or `"both"`), and switches at once.

An endpoint that receives Email events is retried over about 27.6 hours (8 attempts). After a day of failures its owner is told; five days after its first failed attempt, with at least three deliveries given up, Tawked switches it off and says so (Tawked's rule). Turning it on again clears its failures. Endpoints that receive only Verify or WhatsApp events keep their schedule and are never switched off.

`POST /v1/webhooks/{id}/deliveries/{delivery}/replay` sends one final delivery again, delivered or failed, with the same `webhook-id`; `POST /v1/webhooks/{id}/replay` sends again up to 1,000 deliveries of a window of at most 7 days within the last 30. Your receiver may ignore a replay of something it already processed.

A recipient refused by the suppression list produces `email.failed` with `error.code` `recipient_suppressed` and `email.suppressed`: handle one of them. `email.failed` for this cause is kept until a dated deprecation announced at least 90 days ahead.
No existing endpoint receives a new event until its owner adds it; an endpoint created from now starts with every event of its products.
A partner's webhook never receives `email.*`: the events reach the application's own webhook only.
An endpoint receives `email.received` only when it chose it: it is offered beside the sent e-mail's events, and an endpoint made before it arrived does not receive it until you tick it.

`data` is the list item of `GET /v1/email/received`, then `envelope_from`, `message_id`, `in_reply_to`, `authentication`, `parse` (`ready` or `failed`) and `attachments` as `{id, filename, content_type, size, inline, risky}`: no download link, since links expire; fetch the e-mail by its id when you need its content.
The envelope is the Email group's: `type` (equal to `event`) and `timestamp` (when the e-mail arrived) after `data`.
Tawked's own test message to a new address arrives with `"test": true` in the envelope.

balance.low.when: A charge took your balance from at or above your low-balance threshold to below it. Once per crossing: a top-up back above the threshold re-arms it, and a threshold of 0 turns it off.

verification.verified.when: Opt-in. A code was entered correctly. The data is the verification as `GET /v1/verify/{id}` shows it, plus your `external_id`.

verification.failed.when: Opt-in. The attempts ran out, or the send failed.

verification.expired.when: Opt-in. The code expired unused, found by the expiry sweep or by a check.

notes: One webhook for the whole partner account, set under Clients, API and webhook in the console: an HTTPS URL and a signing secret, revealed on demand and rotatable there and nowhere else. The API reads the configuration, chooses the events, sets the low-balance threshold, lists the deliveries and retries a failed one.

Subscriptions decide what reaches the URL: by default every `service.*` event and `balance.low`; the `verification.*` events of your applications are opt-in, one per code, with your `external_id` added to their data. Change the set in the console or with `PUT /v1/partner/webhook`. An endpoint that existed before subscriptions did keeps the five events it always received until you opt in to more.

Every lifecycle and balance event is written to your event log whether or not a webhook delivered it, and the opt-in events when subscribed; `GET /v1/partner/events` reads the log oldest first with a cursor, to poll instead of webhooks or to catch up after an outage. Events and finished deliveries are pruned after 90 days.

The envelope and headers of every Tawked webhook: `{ "event", "data", "sent_at" }` in the body, and the headers `tawked-timestamp` (milliseconds since the epoch, the same value as `sent_at`), `tawked-signature` (hex HMAC-SHA256 of `"{timestamp}.{raw body}"` with your secret), `tawked-event` and `tawked-webhook-id` (one id per event, the same on every retry and on a delivery sent again: dedupe on it). Verify against the raw body before parsing it, and reject old timestamps.

Delivery retries on anything but a 2xx response: 5 attempts in all, the waits between them growing from a minute to hours. The deliveries log under Clients, API and webhook shows every attempt and its response, and lets you retry one by hand.

`data` carries `service_id` and `application_id` (the same value; `service_id` is the legacy name) and your `external_id` on every `service.*` event; `balance.low` is about the account and carries the balance and the threshold.

verification.signature: verify(payload, headers, secrets, { tolerance = 300 s, scheme = "auto" | "tawked" | "standard_webhooks" }); secrets is one string or a list
selection: A secret that starts with whsec_ is only ever used for standard_webhooks; any other secret only for tawked.

auto: when webhook-signature is present and at least one whsec_ secret is given, only standard_webhooks is checked, with the whsec_ secrets; its failure is the answer (no fallback to tawked-signature).

auto: otherwise, when tawked-signature is present and at least one other secret is given, only tawked is checked, with those secrets (a receiver holding only its tawked secret is never failed because Standard headers also arrived).
auto: a signature header present with no secret of its scheme is no_secret_for_scheme; no signature header at all is missing_header.
Timestamps: standard_webhooks in seconds, tawked in milliseconds; the wrong length is malformed_header; tolerance applies to both (|now - timestamp| > tolerance is timestamp_out_of_tolerance).
Constant-time compare over the raw body bytes, never re-serialised JSON.
